categories.name: The World Is Your Dashboard
categories.tagline: Your infrastructure's health, told through Eorzea's sky, crystals and creatures.

ideas.title: The Server Room
ideas.pitch: One glowing panel per homelab node, pinned in your house or to housing furniture, with backlight and derez driven by live health checks.
ideas.experience: Walk down an aisle of Tall Cabinets, each green with a btop or load readout. The NAS stops answering: its panel flickers amber, then red, and your pet swings toward it. Double-click flies you into an ssh session on that box. FC members holding a read-only key see the same wall when they walk in.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, sysadmins, SREs, sysadmin-heavy FCs
ideas.how: Health comes from a hidden capture session or agent probes (ping/tcp/http, node_exporter, incus list) via a new STATUS/EVENT frame, never from the panels, which sleep. Lua maps host to ok/warn/down and sets per-panel tint/backlight; move rez from global host.world_rez to per session in worldview.nelua. Placement uses house-id-aware anchors (see furniture-anchors). Drill-in reuses click focus, fly-in and per-host ssh profiles. Shared view uses read-only guest tokens (see over-the-shoulder-pets).
ideas.risks: No depth test, so panels show through walls. A dozen live btop panels cost real FPS. Housing structs move between patches. Probe flaps cause alert fatigue; this is not a pager. Showing dashboards to an FC leaks hostnames and IPs.

ideas.title: Ops Weather
ideas.pitch: Server health sets your local weather, client-side, so you feel an outage before you read about it.
ideas.experience: All green: Fair Skies. Load climbs and clouds roll in. A failed CI run or degraded pool brings a thunderstorm, rain beads on your panels and a lightning pulse on the failing host's backlight. Fix it and the sky clears.
ideas.audience: sysadmins, homelab folks, SREs, streamers
ideas.how: Agent probe runner sends status over a new EVENT frame. New ops.lua maps states to per-territory weather ids with hysteresis. Shim adds SetWeatherOverride/ClearWeatherOverride beside GetEnvironment using the client-side WeatherManager path Brio and Weatherman use. M.lighting() already reads weather and rain, so tint and backlight follow for free; rain beads drawn in worldview.nelua.
ideas.risks: Not every weather id is valid per territory; houses and duties have none or script their own. Hides real weather from fishers and gatherers, so it needs a toggle and guaranteed restore on unload, zone change and duty. Fights Brio or Weatherman.

ideas.title: Homelab Minion Menagerie
ideas.pitch: Each server gets a client-side creature that follows you and acts out its health.
ideas.experience: Five Proxmox nodes trail you through Gridania. One dozes, one sprints in circles at 100% CPU, one staggers under a smoking box at 95% disk, one plays dead. Click it and its tmux pane opens as a pet terminal.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, sysadmins, collectors
ideas.how: Per-host health records over a new agent frame. Existing place_pet springs drive following. Ready fallback: ImGui billboard sprites on the same springs. Real version: client-side actors via ClientObjectManager or Brio IPC, with a BGCollision raycast for ground height and custom screen-space hit tests.
ideas.risks: Client-spawned actors outside GPose are a known crash source and a grey area; they must despawn before zoning. Brio spawn outside GPose is uncertain. Many actors cost performance.

ideas.title: Aetheryte Uplink
ideas.pitch: Aetherytes become status beacons for your hosts, and teleporting dissolves your terminals into aether that rebuilds on arrival.
ideas.experience: Near an aetheryte, your hosts orbit the crystal as holographic rings with uptime and load, red if down. Cast Teleport and every panel streams into the loading screen, then rebuilds line by line at the destination, scrollback intact.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, sysadmins, anyone who teleports constantly
ideas.how: Shim adds FindNearest(Aetheryte) from IObjectTable. Lua reuses place_pet orbit math; worldview.nelua draws rings and halo. Host data from the shared probe/EVENT feed. Shim forwards Casting and BetweenAreas; worldview runs combat derez in reverse with a screen-space stream during loading and a line-reveal on arrival.
ideas.risks: Halo is faked, not a real crystal tint; rings draw through geometry. Teleport detection is heuristic (Return, duty transitions). Needs a hide-hostnames option on stream.

ideas.title: Airship Departure Board
ideas.pitch: CI/CD pipelines show as airship departures on a split-flap board at the landing or the FC workshop voyage console.
ideas.experience: At the Limsa airship landing a split-flap board rattles to 'deploy/bazzite-sway: BOARDING', then 'EN ROUTE', then 'ARRIVED' in green or 'LOST AT SEA' in red with the failing step.
ideas.audience: developers, DevOps folks, FCs that hang out in the workshop
ideas.how: A world-pinned panel at per-territory coordinates running a `gh run list --json` TUI loop; flip transition per cell in core/render.nelua. Workshop console found by EventObj DataId via a small GetObject extension and pinned like a target anchor.
ideas.risks: Thin novelty over a pinned dashboard. Repo names leak in public spots and on stream, so add redaction. Hardcoded coordinates break on zone changes.

ideas.title: Commit Constellations
ideas.pitch: On clear in-game nights, your git history hangs in the sky as constellations.
ideas.experience: After dark, stars trace your commit graph: branches as trails, merges as clusters, today's commits twinkling. Click one for its message and diffstat; double-click flies into `git show`. Day or clouds hide it.
ideas.audience: developers, open-source maintainers, screenshot hunters
ideas.how: Hidden agent session runs `git log --graph`. sky.lua lays nodes on a camera dome gated by GetEnvironment time, weather and rain. Stars drawn and hit-tested in worldview.nelua with the existing fly-in. Stretch: sky-only occlusion by sampling the depth buffer, as Pictomancy does.
ideas.risks: Without depth occlusion stars draw over rooftops and the illusion breaks. Large graphs don't read as constellations. Decorative and rarely looked at.

ideas.title: Town Criers
ideas.pitch: The NPCs around you start calling out your logs in speech bubbles, so Ul'dah's merchants hawk your warnings and a guard bellows your stack trace.
ideas.experience: `journalctl -f` runs on a minimized panel as you walk into Ul'dah's Sapphire Avenue Exchange, and the merchants start calling out your log: 'Fresh from the kiln, nginx reloaded!' A warning jitters in a yellow bubble over a Brass Blade. When the backup job fails the nearest guard bellows its stack trace in a big red battle-talk frame and every other bubble falls silent.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, streamers, roleplayers with a sense of humour, anyone who tails logs while standing in a city
ideas.how: You pick one session as the crier source and keep it live with run_occluded. The core finds newly written lines from render-state dirty rows and extracts them with ghostty_formatter_format_buf (PLAIN, unwrapped), handing them to Lua, which sorts them by severity with your own patterns. A new shim call walks IObjectTable for EventNpc objects and guard BattleNpcs within about 25 yalms, never players, and returns position and height the way GetObject does today. Lua gives each line to the nearest free NPC with rate limits, and bubbles are ImGui rounded rects projected above each head through the view-projection the world panels already use. Severity picks speech, shaking shout or battle-talk styling, and scripts can shout on purpose with an `ffxiv;crier` APC.
ideas.risks: Screenshots put hostnames and paths over NPC heads. Bubbles ignore depth, show through walls, and can overlap the NPCs' real balloons. Busy cities have dozens of NPCs in range, so cap it at a handful. Players are excluded on purpose, so no one else's character ever appears to say your text, even locally. Long lines must be trimmed and wrapped.

ideas.title: Process Skyline
ideas.pitch: Your machine's process table rises as a neon city on your island: memory sets a tower's height, CPU lights its windows, and every fork raises a new building.
ideas.experience: Fly over your island at night and a city of glowing towers stands in the meadow. Firefox is a 60-yalm skyscraper; `make -j32` throws up a district of cc1plus spires that rise, blaze and collapse within seconds; a zombie process stands as a grey ruin with a small green ghost drifting above it. Hover a tower for its name and PID, double-click it and `htop -p` opens on a panel at its base.
ideas.audience: sysadmins, homelab folks, island decorators, people who like watching builds
ideas.how: A helper on the agent host samples /proc every second and writes the changes as `ESC _ ffxiv;procs;<pid ppid rss cpu state comm> ESC \` into a hidden session kept live with run_occluded, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE with OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES raised. Lua lays out a treemap by parent PID at a `here` anchor, so systemd slices become districts, and tower heights move on the same springs world.lua uses for pets. Towers are extruded quads through world_transform_vertices with windows as lit dotted rects, tinted by world.lighting(). Hovering uses ray-box tests built on the world_hit maths, and double-click opens a panel whose profile runs `htop -p <pid>`.
ideas.risks: Hundreds of processes means hundreds of extruded ImGui boxes, so threads merge, small processes bucket into suburbs and draw calls are capped. Extrusions have no depth test unless routed through the depth pass, so the city shows through hills. Command lines leak tokens in argv, so arguments are hidden by default. On a busy desktop it's just a Chrome city without a filter.

ideas.title: Fishing for Errors
ideas.pitch: Each new kind of error on your machines becomes a fish in the pond, and when you land a real catch it leaps out as a glowing hologram and goes into your Error Guide.
ideas.experience: You sit on the Mist pier with a rod while journalctl churns on the host. You land a Merlthor Goby, and out of the water arcs a three-yalm coelacanth made of text: 'OOMKilled: jellyfin, first seen 02:14, 37 times', fins flickering red. It's a new species, so a NEW RECORD ribbon unfurls and it goes into your Error Guide beside last week's big fish, ECONNRESET.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, anglers, SREs with a sense of humour
ideas.how: On the agent host, `xiv-pond` tails journalctl and app logs, collapses lines into signatures by stripping numbers, hex and paths (drain3-style templates), and writes `ESC _ ffxiv;fish;<sig>;<severity>;<count>;<text> ESC \` into a hidden session kept live with run_occluded. The core captures these through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE and queues them. The shim adds a read of ConditionFlag.Fishing and an IChatGui.ChatMessage filter for your own catch message, and only after that message does Lua pop the most severe queued error. Its leap arc starts at a Raycast point ahead of your facing; severity and count set size and colour. The Error Guide is a ghostty.ui tab saved beside world-state.lua; double-click an entry to open its log on a panel.
ideas.risks: It must never signal bites, hook timing or anything else about the real fish, which would be fishing assistance; it reacts only after the game has told you what you caught. Catch messages differ by client language. Bad templates turn one bug into a hundred species. Log lines carry tokens and hostnames, so redact on the host. It's flavour, not monitoring, so keep a real alert alongside it.

categories.name: Home Is Where the Shell Is
categories.tagline: Housing, chairs and islands turned into workstations and cinemas.

ideas.title: Sit Down to Work
ideas.pitch: Sit in any chair and your panels swing into a seated three-monitor arc while the camera settles into first person.
ideas.experience: You /sit at your study desk. Wall panels spring into a curved arc at seated eye height, unfocused screens dim, the camera eases in. Stand up and everything springs back and your camera is restored.
ideas.audience: developers, roleplayers, cozy-workstation fans
ideas.how: Detect chair sit from ghostty.anim_state() Mode/ModeParam (or forward EmoteController id). Lua 'desk' layout computes arc slots from seated position and heading and springs anchors there. Camera reuses the double-click Get/SetCameraState path, written once and restored once. Model M joins when it lands.
ideas.risks: Tablet/typing pose overrides may knock you out of the chair, so disable them while seated. First-person near-plane clipping. Triggers in inns and public chairs unless limited to housing.

ideas.title: Drive-In Cinema
ideas.pitch: A cinema-sized curved panel on your island or house wall, lit by the game's sunset and rain, optionally broadcast read-only to opted-in friends.
ideas.experience: At dusk you pin a huge screen over the island meadow and start asciinema. Its tint follows the sunset while rain streaks drift across. In the FC house, guests paste an invite code and watch the same live session at the same spot.
ideas.audience: streamers, friend groups, FCs, event hosts, island decorators
ideas.how: Solo works now: /term pin here plus lower pixels_per_yalm and a bigger curve radius; rain streaks from ghostty.env(); per-zone derez opt-out in worldview.nelua. Shared viewing (weeks, stretch): agent broadcast mode that streams output only and rejects DATA/OPEN/CLOSE, through a relay with per-invite keys, anchored by house ward/plot/room.
ideas.risks: Truecolor text video repaints every cell and eats FPS; no kitty/sixel on the cell path. No depth, audio stays on the agent host. Agent token grants a shell today, so broadcast must be a separate read-only relay.

ideas.title: Mount to Furnishing
ideas.pitch: Pin terminals to real housing items, so a painting or bookshelf becomes a screen that moves with the furniture.
ideas.experience: The painting in your apartment shows btop, the bookshelf `journalctl -f`. Drag the painting in the housing editor and the terminal slides along. It returns to the same frame on every visit.
ideas.audience: housing decorators, homelab folks, roleplayers
ideas.how: Shim forwards HousingManager location (house/ward/plot/room) and IndoorTerritory furniture (item id, transform), as MakePlace and BDTH read. New 'furniture' anchor in lua/world.lua matched by item id plus nearest transform, followed every frame, with per-item offset/size from a hand-made table. Replaces zone check with house-id check, since same-size houses share a territory id.
ideas.risks: Panels show through walls and floors without depth; gate by room or height. Structs change with patches and load async. Identical adjacent items confuse matching. Frame fitting needs manual calibration.

ideas.title: Blueprints with Ghost Furniture
ideas.pitch: Share a terminal installation as a paste-able blueprint, or import a MakePlace layout, that projects wireframe outlines where the furniture goes.
ideas.experience: Paste a 'Garlemald Ops Center' blueprint in your Mist apartment and scanline boxes appear where cabinets belong. Place a matching item and it turns solid, its terminal booting with a warm-up flicker after you fill in hostnames and approve each command.
ideas.audience: housing designers, homelab community, content creators
ideas.how: Builds on furniture-anchors. Lua serializes anchors plus item id and relative transform to base64 and imports MakePlace JSON. Nelua draws projected wireframe boxes sized from a per-item table. Match detection by item id within tolerance; template form in views.nelua; warm-up reuses rez.
ideas.risks: Must never write furniture positions: show a match indicator and let the player place. Shared commands are an RCE vector, so never auto-run and hash-pin blueprints. Only transfers between identical house sizes.

ideas.title: Homecoming Boot Sequence
ideas.pitch: Arriving home boots your installation screen by screen and marks what printed while you were away.
ideas.experience: As the loading screen fades, wall screens light up one by one while sessions reattach, with away-time lines tinted amber until you look. Step into the ward and the room folds into a single orbiting pet.
ideas.audience: daily players with long jobs, developers, crafters
ideas.how: Zone-gated anchors and agent replay already exist. Add on_zone_changed in Lua with staggered boot timers, per-session rez in worldview.nelua, an unread row mark in render.nelua set on sleep, and fold-out to one pet when no anchor matches. Per-house layouts need the housing location hook.
ideas.risks: Amber marking fails for tmux and full-screen apps. Mostly presentation over existing persistence. Staggered boot needs a skip.

ideas.title: Saucer Arcade Cabinets
ideas.pitch: Real terminal games run in glowing arcade cabinets along your house wall or beside the Gold Saucer's own machines, with a high-score marquee only you can see.
ideas.experience: A row of cabinets flickers on along the wall of your FC house: crawl, nethack, tint, and a bastet that picks the worst piece on purpose. Double-click one and the camera fills the screen with it. Beat your own best and the marquee bursts into Jumbo Cactpot-style fireworks while the cabinet's light washes over the floor.
ideas.audience: roguelike fans, Gold Saucer regulars, streamers, controller players
ideas.how: Each cabinet is a world panel pinned with `/term pin here` using a profile whose command is the game (crawl, nethack, bastet, tint, moon-buggy, ninvaders). A Lua `cabinet` place() shape tilts the panel back, adds a marquee strip and turns the backlight and light_intensity up. Double-click fly-in already exists. While a cabinet has focus, a keymap mode maps GamepadPressed buttons to arrows and letters through the key encoder with setopt_from_terminal, so DECCKM and kitty flags stay right. The core reads DATA_MODE for synchronized output (2026) and skips render_state_update between begin and end, so fast redraws never tear. The marquee flourish comes from a score-file watcher on the host that writes an `ffxiv;score` APC.
ideas.risks: Dalamud can read gamepad state but can't reliably swallow it, so the stick may still walk your character; keyboard or unused buttons are safer. In the crowded Gold Saucer panels without a working depth test cover other players in your view. 80x24 roguelikes need a readable pixels_per_yalm at fly-in size. Scores are local and easy to fake, which is fine because nothing is shared. It never touches MGP or the real minigames.

ideas.title: The ANSI Gallery
ideas.pitch: Hang classic ANSI art on your house walls, and each piece paints itself at 2400 baud as you walk up to it.
ideas.experience: You walk the upper floor of your apartment past framed 80-column pieces from 1990s art packs. Step within a few yalms of one and it blanks, then paints line by line at modem speed while a faint handshake plays from your desk speakers. A placard below shows title, artist, group and year from its SAUCE record, and next week, with no shell running at all, the wall is still there.
ideas.audience: BBS-era and ANSI art fans, house decorators, retro-computing nerds, streamers
ideas.how: A host tool `ansi-hang` converts .ans files to VT (CP437 to Unicode, iCE colours to bright SGR backgrounds, width from SAUCE), runs the result through libghostty-vt once and saves a GHOSTSNP record with ghostty_snapshot_encode_alloc. In game each frame is a transport-less terminal restored with ghostty_snapshot_decoder_new_buf, so sleep, restarts and the 256 KiB replay ring don't matter. A new lua/gallery.lua triggers the reveal from distance to ghostty.player(): clear the frame, then vt_write the stored VT at a per-frame byte budget (2400, 14400 or 57600 bps presets). Frames are world.lua pins, the placard is a small second panel, and world.lighting() tints them like any panel.
ideas.risks: The renderer doesn't draw blink, and the font needs full block, shade and box-drawing coverage at the right cell aspect or the art looks broken. 80x25 at a readable pixels_per_yalm takes a lot of wall. vt.h warns the snapshot API will change. Link to 16colo.rs rather than bundling art packs. Only you see the gallery, and without the depth test it can show through walls.

categories.name: Body Language
categories.tagline: Your character casts, dresses, gestures and reacts to what the shell is doing.

ideas.title: The Tablet Prop Shows Your Shell
ideas.pitch: The tablet or book your character holds shows your live terminal on the game model itself.
ideas.experience: Zoom in on the tomestone prop in your hands and htop updates on its screen, lit and depth-of-fielded by the game. GPose shots look like you're on call from Eorzea.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, GPose photographers, streamers, sysadmins
ideas.how: Render the terminal to an offscreen texture (ITextureProvider draw-list wrap or D3D11 from Nelua), walk Character to weapon CharacterBase to Material texture, and swap its shader resource view each frame; a Penumbra mod gives a clean UV region. Cheap fallback: forward the hand bone world position and pin a small curved panel there.
ideas.risks: Pointer-swapping game textures risks use-after-free crashes on zoning, redraws and Penumbra reloads. Shared texture shows your shell on every visible instance of that prop. Barely readable outside close-ups.

ideas.title: Commands Cast Like Spells
ideas.pitch: Long-running commands get an FFXIV cast bar and casting pose, and the exit code plays out as a spell effect.
ideas.experience: Run `cargo build --release`: your character raises their weapon into a cast loop and 'Casting: cargo build' fills against its usual runtime. Ctrl+C shatters the bar with 'Interrupted'. Exit 0 plays a chime and /victory; failure throws sparks and an optional /facepalm only you see.
ideas.audience: developers, raiders, streamers
ideas.how: Agent parses OSC 133 C/D in the PTY stream and sends CMD_START/CMD_END frames; OSC 9;4 and 777 via libghostty callbacks as fallback. New lua/cast.lua keeps EWMA durations, a minimum threshold, and picks timelines played through anim_play. Cast bar and particles drawn with ImGui above the projected player. Exit 130 = interrupt. Chime needs a UIGlobals.PlaySoundEffect forward; VFX optional.
ideas.risks: Needs shell integration on every host, tmux passthrough, and remote hooks over ssh. animation.lua's pose guard must yield during casts. Cast timelines vary by job and weapon state. Never touch ActionManager or the real _CastBar.

ideas.title: Wardrobe by Hostname
ideas.pitch: Glamourer IPC dresses you for the machine you're on, so prod looks different from dev.
ideas.experience: `ssh prod-db-01` and you shimmer into a red hazard coat. Homelab tab: loungewear. A sudo prompt adds a crown until it closes. Exit and your glamour returns. Only you see it.
ideas.audience: sysadmins, SREs, homelab folks, glamour enthusiasts
ideas.how: OSC 7 PWD_CHANGED and title give the host; forward on_host(id, host) to Lua. lua/wardrobe.lua maps globs to Glamourer designs for the focused session with ~1s debounce. Shim adds typed forwards for Glamourer apply/revert with a lock key. Sudo from a prompt regex on the cursor row.
ideas.risks: Plain ssh without OSC 7 or titles gives nothing. Glamourer automation can fight the state; crash mid-apply leaves the outfit on. IPC signatures change, so pin the API version.

ideas.title: Emotes as a Window Manager
ideas.pitch: /beckon calls a panel over, /point focuses one, /shoo minimizes it, and bound emotes run commands after confirmation.
ideas.experience: /beckon and your pet springs to your shoulder. /point across the plaza focuses the panel you're facing. /pray is bound to `terraform plan`; a glowing sigil at your feet asks you to confirm.
ideas.audience: nerds, roleplayers, streamers
ideas.how: anim_state() already returns TimelineIds[0]; lua/emotes.lua maps emote timeline ids to actions on rising edge. Point picks the smallest angle off facing. Bound commands go through sendtext.nelua. Sigil is a projected ImGui ellipse. EmoteController.EmoteId forward as backup.
ideas.risks: Pose guard eats emotes within 0.1s, so whitelist them. Confirmation is mandatory and binds default read-only. Slower than hotkeys; mostly for fun.

ideas.title: Flow-State Limit Break
ideas.pitch: Typing fast fills a client-side Limit Break gauge that fires a flourish at your peak.
ideas.experience: A fast pace fills a three-segment LB gauge beside the dropdown with a rising aura. Hold 100 WPM for thirty seconds and your character plays a Limit Break just before `git push`. Stop and it drains.
ideas.audience: developers, streamers, speed typists
ideas.how: Extend animation.lua typing energy with a rolling WPM window and three segments; ImGui gauge; payoff via anim_play of a job LB timeline the pose guard allows. Aura needs an actor VFX forward. Finger IK toward the Model M is dropped.
ideas.risks: LB timelines are job-specific, some long and camera-bound. Rewards typing garbage into a shell. Aura VFX is stretch.

ideas.title: Gaze and Presence
ideas.pitch: Your character turns to the focused panel, startles when a background terminal rings, and dozes after long idle.
ideas.experience: Switch tabs and you turn to face the new panel. A pet behind you rings: you flinch, turn and it pulses. After ten idle minutes you nod off holding the tablet until a keystroke jolts you awake.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, developers leaving builds running
ideas.how: Body turn exists (rate-limited set_rotation); trigger on focus change. Bell already bound in ghostty.nelua; emit on_bell to Lua for a startle timeline, turn and backlight pulse. Doze is an idle timer in animation.lua. Head look-at is research and deferred.
ideas.risks: Merge with the in-progress visual bell rather than building twice. Only rotate while stationary. Look-at conflicts with posing plugins.

ideas.title: Job Codex Terminals
ideas.pitch: The terminal's physical form follows your job: codex pages for Scholar, a star globe for Astrologian, a wrist hologram for Machinist.
ideas.experience: As Scholar your tmux windows are codex pages that flip when you switch windows. Swap to Astrologian and the same session becomes a turning sphere of panes. As Machinist it's scanline hologram off your wrist.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, glamour enthusiasts, one-job mains, streamers
ideas.how: Add ClassJob to GuObject. Lua style table per job selects frame, layout and pose. Nelua render variants: page-flip transition, spherical strip, rune/hologram overlays on existing scanline code. Page flip triggered by tmux window change. Bone anchoring is stretch; pet offset as fallback.
ideas.risks: Per-job art and tuning is a large surface for a niche payoff; ship two or three. Bone positions vary by race and scale.

categories.name: Mail Call
categories.tagline: Finished jobs arrive as moogles, loot and story beats, never mid-pull.

ideas.title: Moogle Mail
ideas.pitch: When a background job, ssh session or tmux alert finishes, a delivery moogle only you can see hands you the result as a letter.
ideas.experience: Crafting in Ul'dah, a moogle flaps in holding an envelope: 'rsync nas -> offsite: complete, kupo!'. Open it and a parchment pane shows the log tail; a failure arrives singed with the stderr. Unread letters collect in a mailbag badge at your hip, and a local chat line 'Your retainer has returned: exit 0, 3m41s' restores the tab on click.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, crafters and gatherers, sysadmins, roleplayers
ideas.how: Triggers: agent EXIT for detached sessions, OSC 9/777 and bell callbacks, plus an agent-side NOTIFY frame so sleeping sessions don't miss completions. mail.lua queues letters (id, title, last N lines), holds them until out of combat and duty, and persists with layout. Parchment theme in render.nelua; letter opens as a pet via place_pet. v1 moogle: ImGui billboard from a game icon texture on pet springs; optional local IChatGui.Print with a link payload. v2: client-side moogle actor (weeks, research).
ideas.risks: Client-side actors crash on zoning and must never spawn in duties or cutscenes. Sprite draws through walls. Needs shell integration or wrappers. Stderr on screen can leak secrets on stream. Share one pipeline with the visual bell and taskbar.

ideas.title: Loot-Roll Job Results
ideas.pitch: Jobs that finish mid-fight wait for combat to end, then drop at your feet as coffers you triage with Need, Greed or Pass.
ideas.experience: `term notify --after-combat make deploy` and you join a hunt train. The deploy finishes during an S-rank; a few seconds after combat a gold or red coffer drops with a chime. Need opens the log as a pet, Greed re-runs, Pass dismisses, all from the gamepad.
ideas.audience: on-call sysadmins, developers with long CI, hunt train regulars
ideas.how: `term notify` asks the agent via a control socket to OPEN a detached session; a PROTO_EVENT frame reports completion. Nelua queues while in_combat and releases after ~5s out. Lua 'drop' anchor springs at your feet tinted by status. Need=ATTACH+make_pet, Greed=OPEN same argv, Pass=CLOSE via existing gesture code.
ideas.risks: Combat flag flickers on trains; debounce. Skip bindings while the game's NeedGreed addon is open. Greed re-running a deploy needs confirmation. ssh-launched jobs need the socket forwarded.

ideas.title: Cutscene Director
ideas.pitch: Long commands finish like a story beat: letterbox bars, a camera move to the panel, and a Talk-style box reading the result.
ideas.experience: Out of combat and standing still, a 4-minute build finishes. Bars slide in, the camera flies to the panel, and a Talk box with the tab as speaker reads 'Build hath completed. 4m12s'. Failures glitch red with an error toast. Any input cancels.
ideas.audience: developers, sysadmins, streamers
ideas.how: Shares the OSC 133 CMD_END frame with cast-bar-commands. Shim forwards BoundByDuty/WatchingCutscene/OccupiedInEvent and IToastGui. lua/director.lua sequences bars, camera (existing fly-in SetCameraState), box and return. Talk box is ImGui with game ULD textures, not the real AddonTalk.
ideas.risks: Unprompted camera moves are jarring; abort on any input or condition change. Needs shell integration. Command names show on stream.

ideas.title: Tomestones for Dead Shells
ideas.pitch: When a process dies its panel falls and leaves a tomestone on the spot, holding an exact snapshot of its last screen and scrollback.
ideas.experience: The overnight `make -j32` in your workshop gets OOM-killed while you're out gathering. When you come home a cracked slab stands where the panel was: 'make -j32, 1h14m, slain by signal 9'. Click it and the panel rises exactly as it died, scrollback and all, and `/tome raise` runs the command again in the same directory once you confirm.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, anyone running long builds, on-call engineers reading a post-mortem
ideas.how: On PROTO_EXIT, Session:mark_exited calls ghostty_snapshot_encode_alloc and writes a GHOSTSNP file beside world-state.lua with territory, pose, argv, cwd (DATA_PWD from OSC 7), title (DATA_TITLE), runtime and status; the agent already reports signals as 128+N. The panel derezzes into a drawn slab with the epitaph. Opening a stone builds a transport-less, read-only Session: ghostty_snapshot_decoder_new_buf, decode to decoder_ready so the final screen draws at once, then decoder_next brings older scrollback in as you scroll. A sleeping panel is detached and never sees EXIT, and the agent drops exited sessions, so the agent must hold a finished session until a client collects it, or link libghostty-vt itself (tools/build.sh already builds the host library) and snapshot at the moment of death. `/tome` is already an alias of `/term`, so `raise` is just a new subcommand.
ideas.risks: Snapshots keep every secret that was on screen: per-profile opt-out, a retention cap and make_private file permissions. vt.h warns the API will change, so version the files and treat old ones as best effort. A graveyard of every `ls` would be silly, so only long runs or non-zero deaths get a stone.

categories.name: Party Up
categories.tagline: Shared screens, pair programming and rituals with your static and FC.

ideas.title: Pass the Model M
ideas.pitch: Pair-program with a party member in one tmux session, and the floating Model M flies to whoever holds the keys.
ideas.experience: /term pair and a curved panel appears between you and your friend with a driver badge in the driver's job color. /term pass and the Model M springs across the gap and clacks in time with their keystrokes. Hand the keys back before the duty pops.
ideas.audience: developers, homelab friends in the same FC, collab streamers
ideas.how: Agent already fans output to multiple attached clients. Add scoped guest tokens (session ids, ro/rw), a per-session driver, and DRIVER/PASS frames over a tailnet. Lua 'between' anchor at the midpoint of player and friend; Model M springs between them on driver events. Each client poses only its own character.
ideas.risks: Guest tokens are a new security boundary on a TLS-less agent, so tailnet only; rw means arbitrary code as the host user. Seeing your friend's pose locally is unproven. Depends on the in-progress Model M.

ideas.title: Over-the-Shoulder Pets
ideas.pitch: Friends who opt in make their orbiting pet terminal visible to you as a live read-only screen.
ideas.experience: Target a friend who shared with you and a cyan outline marks their pet. Focus it and it resolves into their nethack run bobbing by their shoulder. An eye counter on their panel shows viewers; /term min darkens your view.
ideas.audience: streamers, roleplayers, FC mates, roguelike players
ideas.how: Read-only guest tokens scoped to one session plus a PAUSE frame on minimize; LIST already reports attached count. A second AgentClient per share with sessions flagged read-only. Invite carries name@world, matched against target/object table. Generalize the pet anchor to any entity_id.
ideas.risks: Screens may show secrets; needs a clear broadcasting indicator. Skip or clear the 256 KiB replay for guests. Pet positions won't line up exactly across clients.

ideas.title: Static War Room
ideas.pitch: Your static or FC gets one read-only strat board pinned at the same arena wall or FC house spot on every member's client.
ideas.experience: Zone into savage and a curved panel fades in on the north wall for all eight of you. The lead scrolls the strat doc and every copy scrolls. On a wipe, 'pull 47, 6:12' appends to a progression log. It derezzes in combat and returns sharp on the wipe; later the wall switches to the crafters' market dashboard.
ideas.audience: raiders, static leads, FC leadership, progression streamers
ideas.how: World anchors are identical across instances; share as a save_state snippet restored when zone matches (FC house needs HousingManager id). Members attach with read-only guest tokens to a separate broadcast agent; one PTY means scroll sync is free. Shim forwards IDutyState start/wipe/complete; only the lead writes pull number and time. Leader ping is an EVENT frame that turns pets and highlights rows.
ideas.risks: Never parse combat events or show timelines, which would make it a trigger tool. Lead's agent dropping kills everyone's board. Discord screen share covers the basics. Needs opacity for sightlines.

ideas.title: Allagan Terminal Scenes
ideas.pitch: RP hosts and venues run hackable in-world consoles backed by sandboxed scripts that invited players walk up to and use.
ideas.experience: A GM pins a cyan Allagan-styled console in Castrum running a Lua text adventure. Invited players target it and type `override --sector 7`, their characters take the typing pose, everyone in the scene sees the same screen, and the GM replies live. A venue's door kiosk runs a guestbook or drink menu the same way.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, RP venue hosts, event organizers, retro BBS nerds
ideas.how: World anchor shared in the invite. Agent guest tokens with a forced command, like ssh ForceCommand: ATTACH only to the scene session, which runs in a container or restricted user. Client line-buffers and tags lines with name@world. Restricted session mode ignores OSC 52, notifications and hyperlinks. Theme palette plus a licensed fan font via the font atlas. Venue discovery by opt-in directory keyed on ward/plot is research.
ideas.risks: Guests on a host is the core security problem: sandbox mandatory, rate caps, relay to hide IPs. Content sits outside SE moderation. Tiny audience, and non-plugin players see people typing at thin air.

ideas.title: Two-Person Rule by Emote
ideas.pitch: Gate a dangerous command behind signed approvals from party members, with /thumbsup as the ritual.
ideas.experience: `ghostty-gate -- incus delete nas-old --force` shows PENDING, the diff and two empty slots. An FC mate reads it and /thumbsup; their slot fills with name and job icon. The second approval flashes the panel and the command runs as everyone watches.
ideas.audience: sysadmins, SREs, homelab collectives
ideas.how: Authority lives in the agent: held command, quorum policy, approver public keys, ed25519 verify via vendored monocypher over (hash, nonce, expiry), then forkpty. Frames PENDING/APPROVE/APPROVED. Approver's plugin watches only its own timeline for thumbsup (or /term approve), signs and sends over a guest connection.
ideas.risks: Keys inside the game process are readable by other plugins; pitch as oops-prevention, not security, with a hardware-key option. Enforce minimum view time on the diff. Real crypto in a hobby agent needs care.

ideas.title: Paged Mid-Pull
ideas.pitch: When your on-call healer gets paged, opted-in party members see a status line over them, so everyone knows why they went AFK.
ideas.experience: Alertmanager fires and a red line appears over the healer: 'PAGED: disk 97% on nas01'. Their client rings and slides an incident terminal out of their pet slot. When it resolves the line turns green: 'back in 30s'.
ideas.audience: on-call engineers who raid, homelab statics
ideas.how: Webhook receiver pushes a templated STATUS frame to the on-call's agent. Party members hold status-only guest tokens. Map name@world to entity via IPartyList/object table and project an ImGui label above the head. Incident terminal reuses over-the-shoulder-pets.
ideas.risks: Alert text leaks infra details; templated and redacted only. Ship as a mode of over-the-shoulder-pets and the bell, not a separate system. Hide labels in combat.

ideas.title: Linkpearl Bridge
ideas.pitch: Bridge your FC's Matrix or IRC room into a linkshell-styled terminal that echoes lines only into your local chat log.
ideas.experience: An FC mate on a train types 'healer for maps at 8?' in Matrix; it appears locally as [Bridge] in its own color. You reply in weechat. Nothing reaches game chat.
ideas.audience: FC officers, friends split between game and Matrix/IRC
ideas.how: weechat script emits OSC 777 on activity; surface on_notify to Lua (or an agent NOTIFY frame). Shim forwards IChatGui.Print, which is local-only. Lua filters, colors and rate-limits with a clearly non-game tag.
ideas.risks: Low novelty. Chat logger plugins capture external messages. A tag resembling [LS1] invites replying in game chat. Throttle to avoid flooding mid-duty.

ideas.title: Keystroke Colosseum
ideas.pitch: Vimgolf duels fought on two towering arena panels, where every keystroke drains your own HP bar and the stands get instant replays.
ideas.experience: Two FC members face off from opposite pillars in the house courtyard, each under a giant curved panel with the same broken CSV open in vim. Every keystroke knocks a sliver off an HP bar while the stands watch both screens live. Someone lands `:%s/;/,/g` and a floating screen rewinds the last ten seconds for everyone watching. The winner's `:wq` passes the checker and the loser's panel derezzes in a burst of rings.
ideas.audience: vim and emacs zealots, FC game nights, coding streamers, programming clubs
ideas.how: A duel host on the agent opens both contestant sessions from a challenge file inside a container, counts DATA frames per session as keystrokes and runs a checker when the editor exits. Spectators ATTACH to both sessions, and the agent already fans output to every attached client (agent.nelua broadcast). Counts, clock and result arrive as `ffxiv;duel` APCs through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. Lua places both panels with `at` anchors from a shared arena origin and draws HP bars with new ui progress widgets. For instant replay each spectator's client calls ghostty_snapshot_encode_buf once a second per duel terminal into a 15 s ring, and replay decodes each frame with ghostty_snapshot_decoder_decode into a scratch terminal on a replay panel. The derez reuses world.nelua's rez effect and the `burst` bell preset.
ideas.risks: Every attached client can write and there's one token, so contestants need session-scoped tokens and spectators a read-only relay before this is safe. Snapshotting two terminals every second costs CPU and memory, so duel sessions use tiny scrollback. DATA frames don't map one-to-one to keystrokes (escape sequences, key repeat), and paste must be disabled or scored by bytes. Contestants run code on the duel box, so the sandbox is mandatory. Players without the plugin see two people typing at thin air.

ideas.title: Keep Typing and Nobody Derezzes
ideas.pitch: An asymmetric bomb-defusal party game: one player's terminal holds the ticking bomb and everyone else's holds a different page of the manual.
ideas.experience: Your friend kneels at a sparking crate in the FC garden, the only one who can see the bomb terminal counting down from 03:00. You and two others each float a different manual page, one with wire tables, one with a `strings` dump, one with a regex for the serial, and you all yell clues over voice while she types `cut --wire 4`. Wrong wire: the bomb panel glitches, a red sonar ring bursts out of the crate on everyone's screen, and the timer loses 30 seconds.
ideas.audience: FC game nights, Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes fans, event hosts, streamers running viewer games
ideas.how: A game-master script on the host's agent generates a puzzle seed, then opens one bomb session and one manual session per reader. Each invite carries a token scoped to one role's session (read-write for the defuser, read-only for readers) and the crate's anchor as a save_state snippet. The bomb TUI emits `ESC _ ffxiv;bomb;strike=1;t=150 ESC \`, which each client catches through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. Lua turns a strike into a red-tinted `sonar` bell style at the crate anchor, a world.nelua glitch on every panel and a short camera jitter through the existing GetCameraState/SetCameraState path. Detonation plays `burst` and derezzes every panel for a beat. Players talk only over voice or chat they type themselves.
ideas.risks: Scoped and read-only tokens don't exist yet; today's single token grants a shell. Voice chat is effectively required. Puzzle design is real game-design work. The camera jitter needs a motion-sickness toggle and never fires InCombat or BoundByDuty. Guest sessions need the same sandboxing as any shared shell.

categories.name: Between Pulls
categories.tagline: Game-aware QoL for queues, wipes, crafting and the market board.

ideas.title: Queue Pop Eject
ideas.pitch: When the Duty Finder pops, whatever terminal owns your screen lets go, and an opt-in hook lets your desk react.
ideas.experience: Thirty minutes into full-screen vim, the roulette pops. The panel peels off the camera into pet orbit, input returns to the game, and the tab counts down 45 seconds in red. On the host, a hook pauses music and renices your build.
ideas.audience: roulette grinders, developers who queue while working, streamers
ideas.how: Shim forwards IClientState.CfPop duty id via gu_event. Nelua clears world_full_id and stops capturing keyboard. Lua on_duty_pop picks pet or minimize and sets a countdown title cleared on WaitingForDutyFinder/BoundByDuty. Client-to-agent EVENT frame fork/execs an opt-in hook with only DUTY_ID in env.
ideas.risks: Focus not released means you can't press Commence; test hardest. CfPop may miss some queue types. Never auto-commit, never type into the PTY.

ideas.title: Eorzea Cron
ideas.pitch: A crontab on Eorzea time and weather that rings your pet terminal for timed nodes and weather spawns.
ideas.experience: `ecron 'zone=Ruby Sea weather=Thunder ET>=08:00' notify 'Unspoiled node up'`. When the window opens, your pet panel rings. `ecron list` shows the next real-world time for every rule.
ideas.audience: gatherers, mount and minion hunters, cron nerds
ideas.how: Host-side: ET = unix*3600/175, weather forecast from WeatherRate tables in a Lumina/Teamcraft dump, run by a systemd user timer. Notification writes BEL into the pet session; bell already bound. Optional amber pre-pulse via EVENT frame and a tint term in lighting().
ideas.risks: WeatherRate tables change with patches. Island Sanctuary and Occult Crescent don't follow simple rules. GatherBuddy already has alarms; the draw is shell scripting.

ideas.title: Hover-to-Shell Market Board
ideas.pitch: Hovered items stream into your shell, so a Universalis CLI draws cross-world price history beside the retainer bell.
ideas.experience: Open your retainer sell list and a panel beside the bell runs `mb watch`. Hover each item and it redraws a braille sparkline, cheapest listings across your DC and sales velocity. You still set every price by hand.
ideas.audience: market board flippers, crafters, gil-makers
ideas.how: Shim forwards IGameGui.HoveredItemChanged and home DC via gu_event; Nelua debounces ~150ms and relays PROTO_EVENT. `term events --kind hover` feeds a shell script calling Universalis. Panel shown while OccupiedSummoningBell.
ideas.risks: Not every row raises a tooltip. Universalis is crowd-sourced and rate-limited. Existing plugins already show prices; the draw is your own tooling. Never write prices back.

ideas.title: Live Cross Hotbar Shell Slots
ideas.pitch: Hotbar slots bound to shell jobs show live progress rings, so a Steam Deck player can watch a build without opening a terminal.
ideas.experience: Cross hotbar set 8 holds build, ci and backup. A ring fills as `term slot ci progress 0.6` updates; a failure turns the slot red and shakes it. Hold the slot to peek the log tail as a pet, release to send it back.
ideas.audience: Steam Deck and controller players, couch homelabbers
ideas.how: Shim forwards _ActionCross/_ActionBar slot rects plus RaptureHotbarModule and macro text. Nelua maps `/term focus <name>` slots (needs named sessions) and draws rings on the foreground list. `term slot` arrives as PROTO_EVENT. Hold detection from GamepadDown plus active set.
ideas.risks: HUD layouts, WXHB and scale plugins break slot rects. Macro fires on press before hold. Niche for the effort.

categories.name: Showtime
categories.tagline: Replays, redaction, light shows and credits for the camera.

ideas.title: Echo Replays
ideas.pitch: Replay old terminal sessions as ghost holograms in the exact spot they happened, framed like the game's Echo visions.
ideas.experience: Walk back to where you fixed the homelab at 3am and type /term echo. The screen flashes white and a translucent cyan panel rezzes in, replaying the session at real speed. Triggers scrub; /term echo loop 30 loops a stretch for stream.
ideas.audience: roleplayers, streamers, developers
ideas.how: Agent records asciicast-style timestamped output and resizes plus territory and coordinates; REC_LIST/REC_OPEN/REC_CHUNK frames. Replay transport feeds Session:feed on a clock, reusing TermView and rendering. Keyframes every ~5s via libghostty formatter for seeking. Flash, rez-in and ghost tint reuse existing effects.
ideas.risks: Recordings keep every token and hostname printed: retention limits, per-profile opt-out, playback redaction. Disk growth. Keyframes may not restore every mode exactly.

ideas.title: Aetherial Visualizer
ideas.pitch: Audio from a terminal's player makes panel backlights and pet terminals pulse to the beat.
ideas.experience: Start ncmpcpp and panel backlights pulse on the bass, pets kick on their springs, and bars mode raises columns under the panel.
ideas.audience: streamers, roleplayers, venue and club hosts
ideas.how: Agent matches PipeWire nodes to the PTY process tree, captures with pw-record, runs a windowed FFT, and sends 8-16 bands as a BANDS frame at 30-60Hz. Lua modulates backlight and adds pet spring impulses; bars are extra projected quads.
ideas.risks: Audio over ssh plays remotely and can't be captured. Crowds see nothing unless synced. Needs intensity cap and photosensitivity toggle. Flatpak and pulse-compat matching is fragile.

ideas.title: Stream Redaction Mode
ideas.pitch: Streamer mode seals password prompts and secret-looking text on every panel before it's drawn, with an optional Eorzean-script skin for looks.
ideas.experience: Panels keep layout, color and motion, but password prompts, API tokens and IPs become sealed crystal tiles. Panels marked public stay readable. The Eorzean-script skin is style only, since fans can read it.
ideas.audience: streamers, sysadmins, homelab folks
ideas.how: Agent checks tcgetattr after reads and sends SECRET_INPUT when ECHO is off with ICANON. lua/redact.lua regexes dirty rows (ghp_, AKIA, JWT, IPs, *_TOKEN=, key headers); render.nelua draws crystal quads over returned ranges on every surface including the first frame after wake. Cipher skin is a second font handle. Public flag persisted with layout.
ideas.risks: ECHO signal fails inside tmux and ssh, leaving only regex; a missed pattern leaks. Masking must never lag a frame. No hold-to-peek, since OBS captures it. Fan font licensing.

ideas.title: Duty Complete Credits Roll
ideas.pitch: Clearing a duty rolls Final Fantasy-style credits across your pet terminals, written from your session.
ideas.experience: After the clear, the camera orbits your character while pets scroll 'Directed by <alias>', 'Wipes: 14', 'Commands run between pulls: 212', 'Longest command: cargo build, 6m03s', with party members as job icons. Any input skips.
ideas.audience: raiders, streamers, developers
ideas.how: Shim forwards IDutyState and IPartyList ClassJob ids; icons from ITextureProvider. lua/credits.lua builds text from Enter counts and CMD_END durations and feeds generated VT into a local session. Orbit via SetCameraState spring, gated on WatchingCutscene.
ideas.risks: Must not cover the loot window or exit prompt. Default alias must not leak hostname. Duration stats need OSC 133.

ideas.title: OBS Scene Conductor
ideas.pitch: Duty and panel events switch OBS scenes, and stream triggers fire whitelisted cosmetic effects in game.
ideas.experience: Starting a duty switches to your Raid scene and ducks terminal audio; flying a panel full screen switches to Code. Channel-point redeems via Streamer.bot fire a derez burst or spin your pets, and a camera swoop only out of combat.
ideas.audience: streamers
ideas.how: Shim forwards IDutyState and TerritoryChanged; core sends EVENT frames to the agent. A small sidecar speaks obs-websocket v5 and relays inbound events as EFFECT frames. lua/effects.lua maps them to whitelisted calls gated on InCombat and BoundByDuty.
ideas.risks: Viewer camera control is risky if a gate fails. The agent holds another credential and any network exposure widens a shell-granting service. Frame-locked browser overlays are dropped.

ideas.title: GPose Terminal Studio
ideas.pitch: Terminals stay in group pose as frozen props you can scroll back, move, tilt or attach to a character's hand.
ideas.experience: In GPose each panel freezes instead of vanishing. Scroll to an earlier moment, drag or tilt it, or attach it to an actor's hand bone so your character holds the real screen.
ideas.audience: GPose photographers, roleplayers, streamers
ideas.how: Set DisableGposeUiHide; confirm draw callbacks and ViewProjection follow the GPose camera. Freeze via Session:sleep. Drag/rotate gizmo on world_hit/world_unproject. Hand attach via a GetBone shim forward reading hkaPose and a Lua 'bone' anchor.
ideas.risks: ImGui overlays never get game DoF or lighting and cover other actors. The game's screenshot likely excludes Dalamud's layer. Bone math breaks on ClientStructs changes.

ideas.title: Glyphfall
ideas.pitch: Lines that scroll off a world panel fall out of it as real letters that splash in rain, drift in snow and pile up at your feet until you clear the screen.
ideas.experience: Run `find / 2>/dev/null` on a panel in Ishgard and the lines tumble off its top edge as glowing letters, drifting down through the snow into banks around your boots. In La Noscea rain they splash and fizzle, and in a Thanalan dust storm they blow sideways off the cliff. Type `clear` and a gust sweeps the whole pile away in a derez shimmer.
ideas.audience: streamers, screenshot hunters, people who run `yes` for fun
ideas.how: The core keeps a tracked grid ref on the top row of the active area; after new output, that ref's SCREEN position against DATA_SCROLLBACK_ROWS says how many rows just scrolled off, which keeps working once the 10,000-line scrollback is full and the row count stops growing. Each new history row is read back with ghostty_terminal_grid_ref at a HISTORY point plus ghostty_grid_ref_graphemes and ghostty_grid_ref_style, and every non-blank glyph spawns a particle at its cell's spot on the panel's top edge. One Raycast per batch finds the ground, a cheap integrator moves the letters, and they're drawn with PushWorldFont AddText. A new lua/glyphfall.lua turns the ghostty.env() weather id into behaviour: rain splashes and fades, snow drifts and piles, wind and sand push sideways. An empty viewport right after output triggers the sweep.
ideas.risks: Fast output means thousands of letters a second, so it needs a hard particle cap, sampling of every Nth row and whole-line strips as a fallback. ImGui letters ignore depth unless routed through the depth pass, so piles show through walls. Alt-screen TUIs never scroll into history, so htop never snows. Weather ids need a hand-made table, and house interiors have no weather. It's decoration, not a log.

ideas.title: Magic Lantern
ideas.pitch: Aim a panel like a projector and its terminal, text and kitty images alike, is thrown onto whatever it hits: walls, furniture, aetherytes and the people walking through the beam.
ideas.experience: Set a projector at the back of the FC house and run `mpv --vo=kitty trailer.mkv`: the film leaves the glass, covers the far wall, bends over a bookshelf and plays across your own back when you walk through the beam. On a quiet night in Limsa you aim another at the Aetheryte Plaza crystal and htop wraps around its facets. Swing the projector and the image swings with it.
ideas.audience: venue owners, FC movie nights, GPose photographers, streamers, VJs
ideas.how: The projector's terminal is drawn into a texture (ITextureProvider.CreateDrawListTexture from the shim, or a D3D11 render target on the device GuSceneDepth.ui_device already exposes), with kitty images uploaded through the decode path Kitty Graphics Tapestries needs: GHOSTTY_SYS_OPT_DECODE_PNG, re-uploaded when GHOSTTY_KITTY_IMAGE_DATA_GENERATION changes. A full-screen quad then runs through the same draw-list callbacks as core/depthpass.nelua with a sibling of panel_depth.hlsl: it rebuilds each pixel's world position from the reversed-Z SceneDepth and the inverse view-projection rows that cbuffer already carries, moves it into the projector's frustum from its world.place() pose, and samples the texture with cone falloff and a facing term from depth derivatives. app/lights.nelua tints the panel's Scene.Light toward the frame's average colour, so the room's real lighting brightens too. Alt-drag and Shift-snap aim it.
ideas.risks: It adds colour over a finished frame; it isn't real lighting, and it lands behind water, glass and hair that don't write depth. Render-to-texture from the native core is unproven, and the depth path has only been checked in a Wine/DXVK probe. Kitty's shm medium doesn't cross the TCP agent, so video arrives as base64 frames: cap resolution and FPS. Flashing video needs a photosensitivity switch. Only you and your stream see it.

ideas.title: Paint the Sky
ideas.pitch: Pipe a pixel shader from your shell and it replaces the sky over Eorzea on your screen only, fed by Eorzea time, the weather and where your camera points.
ideas.experience: On the Mist lighthouse at dusk you run `aether-sky plasma.hlsl` and the sunset dissolves into a slow demoscene plasma that stops cleanly at rooftops, masts and tree lines. When rain rolls in, the plasma cools to blue and ripples. Swap in a raymarched tunnel and it turns with your camera, so the town seems to sit at the mouth of a wormhole; `aether-sky off` brings the real sky back.
ideas.audience: demosceners, shader artists, streamers, screenshot and GPose folks, venue hosts
ideas.how: A shell helper compiles the HLSL on the Linux host with the same pinned vkd3d-compiler tools/build-shaders.lua uses, so nothing compiles inside Wine, and sends the DXBC as `ESC _ ffxiv;sky;<base64> ESC \`, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE with OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES and OPT_APC_MAX_BYTES raised for the payload. The core checks the DXBC header, creates the pixel shader on GuSceneDepth.ui_device, and adds one full-screen quad at the start of the background draw list through the core/depthpass.nelua callback path, with SceneDepth still bound at t1. The shader keeps only pixels whose reversed-Z depth is 0 (the infinite far plane) and discards the rest. A fixed cbuffer supplies day seconds, rain and weather id from ghostty.env(), the camera-relative inverse view-projection rows panel_depth.hlsl already builds rays from, the depth sizes and the session's bell count.
ideas.risks: Nobody has checked that the sky really reads depth 0; `/term depth show` comes first. A painted sky hides the sun, moon and clouds, and effects that don't write depth leave odd edges. Shader bytecode from a shell runs on your GPU inside the game process, where a heavy shader can stall frames or remove the device, so accept it only from the focused session, time-box it, and ask before loading one from a remote host. Only you and your stream see it.

ideas.title: The Lighting Desk
ideas.pitch: A tracker or cue sheet in a terminal drives a rig of real in-game lights channel by channel, and opted-in patrons at the venue see the same show on their own clients.
ideas.experience: On the stage panel you press play in Furnace: the kick slams a red light up from the floorboards, hi-hats strobe cold blue across the beams, and the lead arpeggio walks a violet spot along the wall, throwing your shadow with it. Mute channel 3 and its spot goes dark mid-bar. The dancer beside you joined the venue's desk at the door, so she /cheers at the same blackout you just saw.
ideas.audience: chiptune and tracker musicians, DJs, dance club and venue owners, event hosts
ideas.how: On the host, `ffxiv-lightd` reads the tracker's MIDI out (ALSA sequencer or JACK) or a cue script and prints `ESC _ ffxiv;cue;ch=1;n=36;v=127;t=183.250 ESC \` into a desk session; the APCs never touch the grid and arrive through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE only on sessions flagged as desks. A new lua/lightrig.lua maps channels to fixtures (offset from a pinned `here` anchor, colour, range, shadows, attack and decay), and app/lights.nelua grows from one light per panel into a capped pool on the same LightCreate/LightUpdate calls (HostApi.cs:400-451). Patrons ATTACH to the desk session: the agent already broadcasts output to every attached client and replays 256 KiB on join. Cues carry desk time, and a new agent timestamp frame lets clients schedule against a playout buffer of about 150 ms. Fixture offsets hang off the house's ward, plot and room, which an in-game MCP server plugin can already read through HousingManager.
ideas.risks: Every attached client can write today and there's a single token, so patrons need a read-only broadcast relay first. Nobody knows how many Scene.Lights the renderer tolerates, so cap the pool at 8-16. Strobes need a hard rate limit and a per-patron intensity slider. Sync is only as good as each patron's latency, and the music reaches them over Discord or Twitch with its own drift. Players without the plugin see a normal club. Aetherial Visualizer pulses panels from local audio; this is an authored, shared show.

ideas.title: Algorave Conductor
ideas.pitch: Live-code music in a terminal and your character conducts at the exact tempo, while the pattern that just played flares on the panel behind you.
ideas.experience: In your FC house you evaluate `d1 $ sound "bd*2 [~ hh] sn"` in Neovim and your character lifts a hand and beats time at 128 BPM. Every drum hit makes the `d1` line flash on the big curved panel behind you, and `d2`'s pads bloom teal half a bar later. Type `hush` and your arms drop as the room goes quiet.
ideas.audience: live coders, algorave and venue hosts, music streamers, roleplayers
ideas.how: TidalCycles and Strudel's desktop setups send every event to SuperDirt as OSC over UDP. A host-side `ffxiv-tidal` reads a mirrored copy of that stream (orbit, cps, cycle, delta, sound) and prints `ffxiv;beat` APCs into a hidden session kept live with run_occluded, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. A new lua/conductor.lua converts cps to BPM and drives ghostty.anim_speed on a pose from animation.lua picked per tempo band, with anim_play flourishes on section changes, all client-side like the existing typing loop. For the flash it finds the row holding `d1 $` on the editor panel with ghostty_search_* and GHOSTTY_SEARCH_DATA_VIEWPORT_MATCHES, then glows that rect in the orbit's colour for the event's delta. Sonic Pi works the same way through its OSC cue log.
ideas.risks: Poses played far off their normal speed look silly, so stick to tempo bands. Tidal doesn't report source spans, so matching an event to its line is a guess; Strudel's events do carry them. The UDP mirror must never add latency to SuperDirt. Animation changes are client-side but stay off in duties. Nobody in the venue sees the code unless they watch your stream.

ideas.title: Cracktro Login
ideas.pitch: Launching the game plays a 1990s cracktro over the title screen: a sine-scrolling greetz list, copper bars, a starfield and a MOD tune from your desk speakers.
ideas.experience: Before you press Start, the logo sky fills with copper bars and a chrome sine scroller: 'GREETZ TO <your static> ... <your FC> ... CODE BY YOU'. A four-channel module thumps from your desk speakers. Hit any key and the intro shatters into the scanline derez, leaving the title menu.
ideas.audience: demosceners, retro-computing fans, streamers, FCs with a sense of humour
ideas.how: The intro is an ordinary terminal program on the agent host: `cracktro` draws truecolor half-block frames (kitty graphics once Kitty Graphics Tapestries lands) and plays the .mod with openmpt123. The core opens it at the title screen, when host.nelua reports not in world and IClientState.IsLoggedIn is false, as a borderless full-screen popup terminal. It holds render_state_update while DATA_MODE shows synchronized output (2026), so each frame presents whole. Greetz come from greetz.txt plus an FC name and friend names cached at your last logout (ClientStructs InfoProxyFriendList; fields to verify). Any key or pad button ends it with the existing derez, once per launch, skippable in settings.
ideas.risks: Full-screen half-blocks at speed are heavy on the per-glyph ImDrawList path. render.nelua doesn't honour mode 2026 today. If the agent isn't reachable before login it must show nothing and never delay the menu. Friends' names on a streamed title screen are a leak, so friend greetz are opt-in. Copper bars need a calm preset, and MOD files carry their own licences.

categories.name: Nerd Power Tools
categories.tagline: SSH, CI and git dressed in game mechanics that actually do work.

ideas.title: Aetheryte Network for SSH
ideas.pitch: Your ~/.ssh/config becomes a teleport menu, and connecting casts a client-side teleport that lands a shell beside you.
ideas.experience: ctrl+t opens an Aetheryte-style host list grouped by ProxyJump chain, RTT as cost, unknown hosts unattuned. Pick one: your character casts, the current panel derezzes, and a pet lands at the remote prompt. Expand a host to attach its tmux sessions as shards.
ideas.audience: sysadmins, homelab folks, anyone with too many SSH hosts
ideas.how: New Nelua primitive ghostty.run(argv, cb) capture session plus ghostty.command(text). Agent-host helper prints TSV from `ssh -G`, `ssh-keygen -F` and a TCP connect time; tmux shards via ControlMaster only on expand. Lua menu in core/ui.nelua table widget; anim_play cast timeline, derez, open `ssh -t host` and pin as pet. No shim changes.
ideas.risks: Can't hijack the real Teleport keybind. Probes can trip 2FA, fail2ban or slow DNS, so TCP connect only. Cast timeline must not lock movement. Real teleport VFX is research.

ideas.title: Deploy as a Raid Pull
ideas.pitch: CI jobs show as party frames, and a production deploy needs a charged Limit Break hold before Enter goes through.
ideas.experience: The GitHub Actions run shows as party frames: HP is steps done, cast bar the current step, enrage the timeout, debuff icons on failures that open `gh run view --log-failed`. Type `terraform apply` and Enter becomes a three-segment LB gauge you hold to fill. Green runs play victory.
ideas.audience: developers, DevOps engineers, raiders
ideas.how: Capture session polls `gh run list/view --json` every ~10s to TSV; frames drawn with new ui.* progress widgets. ghostty.input_line(session) reads cursor-row cells with SEMANTIC_CONTENT==INPUT (OSC 133). keymap.lua swallows Enter on guarded patterns until the hold fills, then sends \r. Victory via anim_play, skipped while BoundByDuty.
ideas.risks: A speed bump, not a safety control: needs OSC 133 and is bypassed from any other terminal. Swallowing Enter needs a visible reason and Esc to cancel. gh rate limits.

ideas.title: Parse Your Shell
ideas.pitch: An ACT-style meter ranks your session's commands by time and colors each like an FFLogs parse.
ideas.experience: Your slowest `nix build` is grey, a quick test run purple, your best `make check` gold. Failed commands get death markers. Click a row to jump to that prompt's output; copy a text summary to paste wherever you like.
ideas.audience: raiders who are developers, performance nerds
ideas.how: Agent parses OSC 133 with libghostty's standalone OSC parser and timestamps an EVENT frame delivered even to detached sessions. Lua keeps per-command history and percentiles and draws colored bars. Jump scans rows for SEMANTIC_PROMPT. Summary via SetClipboardText only.
ideas.risks: Needs OSC 133 through tmux and ssh. Scrollback lost on sleep/restart. Percentiles mean little with few runs. No automated chat sends.

ideas.title: Git Status as Buffs and Debuffs
ideas.pitch: Each pet terminal gets a mob-style nameplate with its branch and a buff row for repo state.
ideas.experience: Your pet reads 'feature/observatory <bazzite-sway>' with the last exit code as its level. Below: a stack count of dirty files, ahead/behind arrows, a crystal per stash, and a pulsing Doom icon during a merge conflict. Click Doom to type `git status`.
ideas.audience: developers who live in git
ideas.how: precmd hook runs `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` with a timeout and emits a private OSC user var. Wire UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE in session.nelua to Lua on_uservar. worldview projects the nameplate above each pet via a world.nameplate(id) hook; click uses /term type.
ideas.risks: Slow git in big repos adds prompt lag. Check whether OSC 1337 SetUserVar reaches the callback; else use an unused OSC number. Overlapping nameplates, stale state while asleep.

ideas.title: The Failing Suite (Extreme)
ideas.pitch: Target a striking dummy and your test suite becomes a trial boss: failing tests are its HP, compiler errors pull as adds on an enemy list, and all green plays Duty Complete.
ideas.experience: You target the dummy in your FC workshop and type `/term trial pytest`. Its nameplate becomes 'The Failing Suite (Extreme)', a boss bar reads 28 failing of 240, and the worst traceback towers behind it on a hologram panel like a primal. Save a fix and yellow '+17' numbers fly off the dummy while 'E0308 mismatched types: loader.rs' aggros onto the enemy list; click it and nvim jumps to line 214. At zero the hologram shatters in a scanline derez and a Duty Complete banner sweeps the screen.
ideas.audience: developers who practise TDD, compiled and typed language folks, streamers who code, raiders with a CI habit
ideas.how: A host wrapper runs the suite and the checker under watchexec, reads JUnit or JSON output (`cargo check --message-format=json`, `tsc --watch`, `ruff --output-format json`) and prints `ESC _ ffxiv;suite;pass=..;fail=..;fixed=..;top=<test> ESC \` plus `ffxiv;diag;<json>` snapshots, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE (session.nelua sets neither option today). A new lua/trial.lua diffs snapshots into damage, new adds and kills, ranks adds with primary errors first, and keeps a local hunt log. The hologram is a world panel on the existing `target` anchor raised above the dummy, running `less +G` on the top failure. Boss bar, enemy list and banner are ImGui in chrome.nelua's glass style; numbers go through a new shim call to IFlyTextGui.AddFlyText, and the nameplate is renamed in INamePlateGui.OnNamePlateUpdate only for a BattleNpc whose BNpcName is a striking dummy. Clicking an add writes `goto file:line` to the wrapper, which calls `nvim --server $NVIM --remote-send`.
ideas.risks: Hitting the dummy puts you in combat, and combat derezzes everything, so this is a boss you watch, not one you fight. AddFlyText may only attach to your own character, so the dummy's numbers might have to be drawn by the plugin. One refactor can spawn 300 adds, so cap and roll them up, and crediting a root-cause fix with its cascade is a heuristic. Giant tracebacks carry paths and secrets. It's gated to dummies outside duties so it never looks like a real combat HUD.

ideas.title: Debugger Trial: The Floor Is the Source File
ideas.pitch: Attach a DAP debugger and your source file unrolls across the ground as a boss arena: breakpoints are AoE telegraphs, the current line is a tank-buster marker and an uncaught exception is a wipe.
ideas.experience: `/term trial python -m pytest -x` and the arena rezzes around your feet: `solver.py` lies flat as the floor, breakpoint lines ringed in orange telegraphs, the call stack standing at the north edge like a boss timeline. F10 slides the glowing marker down the floor, and changed locals pop out of their lines as flytext: 'retries 2 -> 3'. Step into a call and the floor derezzes and rebuilds as `http.py`. Then the exception: the screen flashes red, 'ENRAGE: KeyError token' crawls across the arena, and the frame that threw glows.
ideas.audience: developers who live in debuggers, raiders, live-coding streamers
ideas.how: A host-side `ghostty-dap` runs as a small REPL in its own session and speaks DAP to debugpy, lldb-dap or `dlv dap`. On every `stopped` event it writes `ESC _ ffxiv;dap;<base64 JSON> ESC \` with file, line, breakpoints, stack and changed variables, forwarded to a new Lua hook through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE. The floor is a second world panel placed with pitch -90 through the placement table, running `bat --paging=never` on the file; world_axes and the depth-pass basis already tilt with pitch. Telegraphs reuse the ring renderer in app/bell.nelua projected onto the floor's rows, and the stack is a pet panel. A new keymap action sends F5, F9, F10 and F11 to the ghostty-dap session whichever panel has focus. The arena refuses to open while BoundByDuty and derezzes in combat like every panel.
ideas.risks: A floor-sized panel adds real overdraw, and no panel has been laid at -90 degrees yet, so it floats slightly above the ground to avoid z-fighting. Reading text at a steep camera angle is the hard part, and first person may be the only readable view. APC through tmux needs passthrough. Every DAP adapter has quirks. It stays a toy until conditional breakpoints and watches exist.

ideas.title: Git Bisect, Heaven-on-High
ideas.pitch: `git bisect` becomes a deep-dungeon descent, one floor per step, ending in a boss room where the first bad commit is waiting.
ideas.experience: `git bisect start HEAD v1.2` and a floor counter drops in over your pet terminal: 'Heaven-on-High, Floor 1 of ~7, 97 commits remain'. Mark a commit good and a Cairn of Passage lights blue as you sink a floor; bad springs a trap; `skip` spends a Pomander of Safety. Under `git bisect run` the floors flash past in a few breaths. Floor 7 locks shut and a boss nameplate reads 'c41e9d0: hot-swap loader cleanup, 3 weeks ago', with its diff on the panel behind it.
ideas.audience: developers hunting regressions, Deep Dungeon grinders
ideas.how: A precmd hook, plus a `git` wrapper for run mode, checks for .git/BISECT_LOG. When it's there, the hook takes bisect_nr and bisect_steps from `git rev-list --bisect-vars` over the bad and good refs, reads the last verdict from `git bisect log`, and spots the `# first bad commit:` line that log gains when the hunt ends. It prints `ffxiv;bisect;floor=..;left=..;verdict=..` as an APC, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE (the Stage Directions plumbing). A new lua/bisect.lua maps good, bad and skip to cairn, trap and pomander effects built from bell.lua rings and the worldview glitch and derez, and on the boss floor pins a panel running `git show --stat` beside the pet.
ideas.risks: It's a theme on top of real work. The precmd hook never fires inside `git bisect run`, so run mode depends on the wrapper. Floor estimates wobble with skips and merges. Deep Dungeon art is limited to game icons through ITextureProvider.GetFromGameIcon and colour. APC through tmux needs passthrough.

ideas.title: Blue Magic: Learn Commands by Watching
ideas.pitch: When a pair, an agent or a teammate's panel runs a command you've never typed and it works, you learn it like Blue Magic into a spellbook you can cast from later.
ideas.experience: Claude, fixing the agent, runs `journalctl --user -u ghostty-agent -g token --since -1h` and it works. Blue motes spiral off its panel into you: 'You learn Journal Scry (No. 37)'. A week later you open the spellbook's grid of icons and pick Journal Scry; the command appears at your prompt with `ghostty-agent` and `-1h` selected as placeholders, waiting for your Enter. Spells you never cast fade to grey.
ideas.audience: developers learning from pairs and AI agents, Blue Mage mains
ideas.how: Commands come from two sources. Any shell with OSC 133: the text is read from cells whose GHOSTTY_CELL_DATA_SEMANTIC_CONTENT is INPUT between prompt rows, with the exit code from the agent-side CMD_END frame proposed in Commands Cast Like Spells, since libghostty-vt drops it. And Claude Code: PostToolUse hooks on its Bash tool emit the command and whether it errored. A host helper `ghostty-spellbook` checks $HISTFILE or atuin to decide whether a command is new to you, redacts secret-shaped arguments and turns paths and numbers into placeholders. A new lua/bluemage.lua stores spells, names them from a small word list keyed by binary, draws the book with ghostty.ui widgets and plays the motes over the source panel. Casting goes through `/term type` into the focused session, never `/term send`.
ideas.risks: A command working for an agent doesn't make it safe, so destructive verbs (`rm`, `dd`, `git push --force`, `terraform apply`) can never be learned, and casting never presses Enter. argv often carries secrets, so redaction is conservative and the spellbook file is made private. The naming whimsy wears off, so plain names are an option.

ideas.title: Palace of the Dead Inodes
ideas.pitch: Your filesystem becomes a dungeon you walk: directories rise as doorways around you, files sit as coffers, and walking through a door cds the shell or leaves a permanent door in your house.
ideas.experience: `/term crawl ~/src` and 'Floor 3: ~/src' flashes across the screen as a ring of doorways rises, one per subdirectory. Walk up to a coffer and it opens into a `bat` preview, and the 4 GB core dump lurking among them is a mimic. Walk through 'ghostty-dalamud' and the ring collapses, the shell cds, and the next floor rezzes in around you. Back home, Alt-drag a folder link out of `ls --hyperlink=auto` and its arch stays on your apartment floor, a door into that repo that's still standing tomorrow.
ideas.audience: developers lost in monorepos, people teaching the shell, housing decorators who want a repo room, Deep Dungeon enjoyers
ideas.how: A host helper `xiv-crawl` prints `ESC _ ffxiv;floor;<json: names, kinds, sizes> ESC \` after each cd, caught through OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE, while OPT_PWD_CHANGED and DATA_PWD confirm where the shell really is. Lua places doors on a ring around ghostty.player() at Raycast ground height, and a segment test on consecutive player positions detects a crossing, which sends `cd -- 'name'` through the `/term send` path only while DATA_CURSOR_AT_PROMPT (OSC 133) is true. Permanent doors come from OSC 8: map the mouse cell to a grid ref, check GHOSTTY_CELL_DATA_HAS_HYPERLINK, read ghostty_grid_ref_hyperlink_uri, accept only file:// links whose host matches the agent's (a hostname added to its OK reply), and save the arch per zone in world-state.lua. Crossing a saved door OPENs a new panel with a PWD env entry, which the agent already chdirs on. Coffers are small preview panels; `..` is the exit portal.
ideas.risks: Needs open floor such as a house, the island or an empty field, and walls clip doors. Huge directories need paging into floors of about 20. The agent has no stat or hostname today, and file:// links printed over ssh point at other machines. Walking must always be your own movement: the walk-up steering hook must never carry you through a door. Not for use inside a real Deep Dungeon.

categories.name: Terminal Craft
categories.tagline: Making the emulator itself excellent in three dimensions.

ideas.title: /grep the World
ideas.pitch: One scrollback search across every terminal you own, with hit counts floating over panels and 'next' flying the camera to the match.
ideas.experience: /term find OOMKilled and every panel with a match gets a '3' badge and a soft pulse, including the pet at your shoulder. Next turns the camera to the panel, scrolls and highlights the line. On controller, the d-pad steps between shell prompts.
ideas.audience: sysadmins, homelab folks, on-call engineers who raid
ideas.how: libghostty-vt ships vt/search.h with incremental feed/tick across screens and scrollback. One GhosttySearch per Session, a few ticks per frame. Highlight as selection, scroll via scroll_delta, badges projected in draw_world, counts in the Umbra popup for minimized tabs. Camera reuses fly-in easing; prompt stepping via SEMANTIC_PROMPT.
ideas.risks: Sleeping panels only retain the 256 KiB replay ring; search agent-side or say so plainly. Byte-exact matching, no regex. Prompt stepping needs shell integration.

ideas.title: Folding Screen Splits
ideas.pitch: Splitting a world terminal hinges it into a folding screen of panes you can angle, fold shut and walk around.
ideas.experience: ctrl+shift+\ creases a world panel down the middle: vim on the left leaf, tests on the right. Split again for a triptych around your desk with the focused leaf lit. Drag a hinge to open flat or fold a leaf shut while its process keeps running.
