ideas.audience: tmux addicts, sysadmins, housing decorators, roleplayers
ideas.how: Each leaf is its own Session; add group id and leaf index to layout persistence. Lua computes leaf placement from the group anchor with hinge yaw animated by spring(). No new projection math. Hinge drag is a new grip mode calling policy_world_hinge. Folded leaves sleep via sleep_unseen. /term split and fold commands.
ideas.risks: Overlapping leaves need depth-sorted picking. Long-folded panes lose older scrollback on wake. Resizing a leaf must rebalance neighbours.

ideas.title: Kitty Graphics Tapestries
ideas.pitch: Kitty graphics protocol images render on 3D panels, so live dashboards and pictures hang in the world like paintings.
ideas.experience: `watch -n30 'curl grafana/render/... | kitten icat'` on a panel pinned to your house wall and a live Grafana graph hangs there as a curved tapestry, tinted by time and weather. It returns with a scanline wipe when the panel wakes.
ideas.audience: homelab folks, streamers, venue decorators
ideas.how: libghostty-vt already implements kitty graphics placements. Decode PNG with vendored stb_image or Zig. Shim forwards CreateTexture/ReleaseTexture via ITextureProvider.CreateFromRaw, cached by image id. Draw placements as tessellated quads so world_transform_vertices curves and tints them; plain AddImage in 2D. No sixel.
ideas.risks: Images vanish past the replay ring on sleep or restart unless re-sent or cached agent-side. Cap texture memory in-process; create on the render thread and free on unload or crash.

ideas.title: Item Links in stdout
ideas.pitch: OSC 8 links with an ffxiv:// scheme turn CLI output into item tooltips, map flags and chat-ready item links.
ideas.experience: A crafter script prints 'Grade 8 Tincture of Strength x3 @ 4,200g'. Hover for an icon-and-stats tooltip, ctrl+click to put a real item link in your chat input to send yourself, or click coordinates to drop a map flag.
ideas.audience: crafters, gatherers, market goblins, CLI tool authors
ideas.how: Mouse to cell to GhosttyGridRef, then ghostty_grid_ref_hyperlink_uri, sharing mouse-selection plumbing. Lua parses item/map/quest URIs into typed actions. Shim forwards Lumina Item lookup and icon, OpenMapWithMapLink, and a chat-input item link insert. ImGui tooltip first; native tooltip later.
ideas.risks: Output is untrusted: typed actions only, click required, never free text into chat. Chat-input insertion depends on unstable ClientStructs internals.

ideas.title: Legible at 40 Yalms
ideas.pitch: Distance LOD for world panels: full text up close, block minimap rows mid-range, a one-line nameplate far away.
ideas.experience: htop on a Limsa pillar is crisp up close. Walk away and lines become colored blocks shaped like the text; further, the panel collapses to a nameplate: 'build passed 3m12s'. Distant panels also get cheaper.
ideas.audience: developers, sysadmins, screenshotters, streamers
ideas.how: draw_world already has projected corners; divide by rows for on-screen cell height and pick glyphs, run blocks (reuse the merged background-run loop), or nameplate from title, last row or OSC 9;4 progress. Lua owns thresholds with hysteresis. Font mip handles at 20/40/80px chosen in PushWorldFont. MSDF is research.
ideas.risks: No ligatures: per-cell AddText, no shaper. Big font atlases grow fast. LOD pop needs cross-fade.

ideas.title: Soul Crystal Themes
ideas.pitch: Terminal palettes re-derive live from your job, HUD theme and chat colors, and the prompt can show the real job icon.
ideas.experience: Swap from WHM to DRK and every terminal crossfades to a palette from the job color, diff additions in FC-chat green, errors in Tell pink. Your starship prompt shows the job as the game icon.
ideas.audience: developers, job-swapping raiders, ricers, streamers
ideas.how: Set GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_COLOR_PALETTE with a per-frame lerp; lua/theme.lua builds 16 colors with a contrast clamp while app OSC overrides still win. Shim forwards ClassJob, ClassJobChanged and IGameConfig HUD/chat colors. Job icon drawn as a texture at a placeholder codepoint; prompt queries job via custom OSC.
ideas.risks: SeIconChar shares the PUA with Nerd Font powerline glyphs and ImWchar is 16-bit, hence textures. Job colors have poor contrast without clamping. Config option names need checking.

ideas.title: Parse Your Terminals
ideas.pitch: A /term perf meter colors each terminal's frame cost like a DPS parse, and a governor tightens budgets inside duties.
ideas.experience: /term perf shows draw ms, vertices and PTY bytes/sec per tab: grey at 0.3ms, pink for the cmatrix tab burning 4ms. Entering a duty throttles unwatched panels ('budget 1.5ms, 2 throttled'); GPose lifts all caps.
ideas.audience: raiders, performance nerds, streamers, low-end laptops
ideas.how: QueryPerformanceCounter around draw_terminal and world_transform_vertices, vertex deltas, byte counters per session. Governor caches flat panel geometry and on throttled frames skips render_state_update and render_termview, re-running only the transform. Shim forwards BoundByDuty, IsGPosing and local chat print.
ideas.risks: Stale geometry cache after resize or font change draws garbage. Combat derez already cuts much of the duty cost. Chat notice should be opt-in.

ideas.title: Inherits Your Accessibility Settings
ideas.pitch: The terminal follows the game's color-blindness filter, supports accessible fonts per tab, and can speak matching output lines.
ideas.experience: With deuteranopia filter on, red/green diffs become blue/orange. Tabs can use Atkinson Hyperlegible or OpenDyslexic. A tab marked spoken reads lines matching ERROR aloud, so a failing deploy is audible mid-pull.
ideas.audience: colorblind, low-vision and dyslexic players, raiders who can't look away
ideas.how: CVD-safe palette preset chosen from a forwarded IGameConfig color-filter option. Per-profile font handles via AddFontFromFile. Agent strips escapes, regex-matches lines and sends a small frame; speech via host-side piper/espeak, SAPI or TextToTalk IPC as options.
ideas.risks: No global high-contrast mode to inherit; offer a manual AAA palette. SAPI under Wine is poor, so prefer host TTS. Rate-limit speech so it never talks over callouts.

ideas.title: Kana on the Curve
ideas.pitch: IME composition text renders inline at the cursor, even on curved world panels, with a game-styled candidate list.
ideas.experience: A Japanese player types into nvim on an apartment panel: composition text appears underlined at the cursor, bending with the panel, and kanji candidates pop out beside it. Same in the dropdown, ssh and tmux.
ideas.audience: JP/CN/KR players, multilingual developers, roleplayers
ideas.how: Committed text and wide cells already work. Shim hooks WM_IME_COMPOSITION/ImmGetCompositionString (or reflects into Dalamud) to forward preedit and cursor. render.nelua draws the underlined overlay in the same draw range so world_transform_vertices curves it. Candidate frame is ImGui; merge a CJK font subset.
ideas.risks: CJK at 40px bloats the atlas; ImWchar is 16-bit so no astral characters. IME through Wine/Proton on Linux is unreliable. WndProc hooks can conflict with Dalamud's IME.

ideas.title: Apps That Follow the Sun
ideas.pitch: The terminal tells your apps it's light mode at Eorzean dawn and dark mode at dusk, so their themes change as the sun comes up over Thanalan.
ideas.experience: You're editing on a pet terminal in Ul'dah at 5:58 ET. The sun clears the walls, the glass warms, and on the same beat Neovim and every other app listening for colour-scheme reports switches to its light theme without a keypress. Step into a dungeon or your basement workshop and everything goes dark again; a thunderstorm keeps it dark until the storm passes.
ideas.audience: Neovim, Helix and fish users, readability-sensitive players, anyone who plays at odd hours
ideas.how: A Lua hook scheme.decide(env) reads ghostty.env() (day seconds, rain, weather id) plus an indoors flag the shim would add from TerritoryType, and returns light or dark with hysteresis. Sessions register GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_COLOR_SCHEME so `CSI ? 996 n` queries get the current answer. When the answer flips, every session whose DATA_MODE shows 2031 gets an unsolicited report from ghostty_color_scheme_report_encode written to the PTY. OPT_COLOR_BACKGROUND, FOREGROUND and PALETTE switch to dawn and dusk sets built with ghostty_color_palette_generate and clamped with ghostty_color_contrast, so tools that only query OSC 10/11 at startup get the right colours next launch. Sleeping panels get the latest report on wake.
ideas.risks: Mode 2031 support is uneven, and many tools read OSC 11 once and never again. A mid-session flip can be jarring, so it's per profile with a manual override and flips at most once per Eorzean hour (about three real minutes). Reports only go to apps that enabled 2031, never into a bare prompt. Soul Crystal Themes recolours the terminal; this tells the apps.

ideas.title: Allagan Phosphor
ideas.pitch: Every terminal re-renders in the technology of wherever you stand: Allagan green phosphor, Garlean magitek amber, Sharlayan hologram blue, Crystarium cut glass.
ideas.experience: Zone into Azys Lla and your btop panel flickers into a curved green Allagan readout, scrolling logs leaving faint phosphor trails. In Garlemald it warms into a rounded amber magitek CRT with a hum bar crawling up the glass. In the Crystarium the slab turns to cut crystal that bends the plaza behind it with rainbow fringes, and a failing build sends a hairline crack across it that seals on the next exit 0.
ideas.audience: ricers, lore fans, roleplayers, GPose folks, retro-computing fans
ideas.how: Draw each world panel's cells into an offscreen texture with ITextureProvider.CreateDrawListTexture, only when the render state reports GHOSTTY_RENDER_STATE_DIRTY_PARTIAL or FULL, so idle panels cost nothing. Draw that texture on the curved quad through the core/depthpass.nelua callbacks with a material shader built by tools/build-shaders.lua: barrel curvature, shadow mask, scanlines, bloom, and persistence blended with last frame's texture. The glass material also copies the panel's screen rect from the back buffer and offsets its samples by the cylinder normal panel_depth.hlsl already computes. A new lua/materials.lua maps TerritoryType through Lumina to material tables, world.place gains a `material` field, and zone changes crossfade. While DATA_MODE shows synchronized output (2026) the texture keeps its last frame so trails never smear a half-drawn screen. Cracks key off the agent-side CMD_END exit code.
ideas.risks: Render-to-texture adds a pass and texture memory per dirty panel, and it's unconfirmed that CreateDrawListTexture accepts a draw list built by the native core, so a direct-draw fallback stays. The back-buffer copy is taken after the HUD is drawn, so HUD pieces behind glass bend too. Curvature and bloom cost legibility, so a hold-to-read key snaps back to crisp. Persistence trails can bother motion-sensitive players. Nothing on the depth path has been observed in game.

ideas.title: The Scrollback Spire
ideas.pitch: A terminal's whole scrollback rises out of the ground as a tower of text you fly up to read, and every screen of output adds a storey.
ideas.experience: On your island a slim spire of glowing rows climbs out of the grass, with the live screen at its base. A long build pushes it higher as you watch. Mount up and fly along it: 80 yalms up you're reading yesterday's apt upgrade, and a lit ledge marks the bookmark you left at the first error. Click the ledge and the panel at the base scrolls straight to that line.
ideas.audience: sysadmins tailing logs, streamers, flying-mount collectors, anyone who has lost output
ideas.how: The base is an ordinary pinned panel. For the rows above it the core reads history with ghostty_terminal_grid_ref at HISTORY points, sized by DATA_SCROLLBACK_ROWS and DATA_TOTAL_ROWS, and caches each row's text once when it scrolls off. Only the band within about 40 yalms of camera height is drawn through world_transform_vertices, with block LOD above and below. Rows sit on a vertical cylinder, so the existing curve and hit maths apply. Bookmarks are tracked grid refs (ghostty_tracked_grid_ref_*), which survive reflow and go empty when pruned. Clicking a ledge calls ghostty_terminal_scroll_viewport with ROW. A new shim read of ConditionFlag.InFlight fades in the upper storeys only while you fly.
ideas.risks: At a readable size 10,000 lines is about 200 yalms, so it needs a height cap or compressed storeys. A sleeping panel only has the 256 KiB replay ring, so the spire shrinks after wake unless rows are cached on the client. Flying only works in some zones, and on the island after unlocks. Distant rows cost FPS without strict LOD. Old secrets in scrollback become readable from across the map, though only to you.

categories.name: Protocol Alchemy
categories.tagline: Escape sequences that climb out of the glass and become things you can hold.

ideas.title: Stage Directions in the Byte Stream
ideas.pitch: A private `ESC _ ffxiv;` escape lets your scripts and TUIs cue real lights, bell rings, poses and camera moves on the same frame as the text they print.
ideas.experience: Your homemade text adventure prints 'The lantern gutters out.' and on that frame the real light beside your panel dies, a grey wash crosses the glass and a low sonar ring rolls out from your feet. deploy.sh ends with `stage cam=push-in bell=burst`, so the camera eases onto the panel just as LIVE appears. `cat` a stranger's log and nothing happens, because that profile isn't trusted.
ideas.audience: storytellers, RP venue hosts, streamers, demoscene nerds, anyone who writes shell scripts for fun
ideas.how: Profiles with `stage = true` set GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_UNKNOWN_SEQUENCE and a 4 KiB OPT_UNKNOWN_MAX_BYTES; libghostty-vt then hands over every APC it doesn't handle itself (kitty `G` and the glyph protocol stay internal), and the callback keeps only `ffxiv;v=1;` payloads. A new Lua hook, stage.cue(id, verbs), maps a whitelist onto what already exists: app/lights.nelua colour and intensity, bell.lua presets, world.place tint and backlight, anim_play, and showcase-style SetCameraState shots. While DATA_MODE reports synchronized output (2026), cues queue and fire when it clears, so a frame and its effect land together. An `ffxiv;q` probe is answered through the session's WRITE_PTY path so scripts can detect support, and a tiny `stage` shell helper ships beside ghostty-agent. Most of the APC-driven ideas in this batch stand on this plumbing.
ideas.risks: Output is untrusted: an ssh session to a hostile box, or a log you cat, could flash lights or yank the camera, so it's off per profile by default, with a verb whitelist and a rate limit. Cues arriving in reattach replay are dropped, the way replayed bells already are. Camera and pose verbs are refused in combat, duties, cutscenes and GPose, and there will never be movement, targeting, chat or command verbs. tmux drops unknown APC unless allow-passthrough is on and the sequence is wrapped.

ideas.title: Clipboard Crystals
ideas.pitch: Every OSC 52 copy buds off the panel as an aether crystal that orbits you, and a remote program can read your clipboard only while you hold one out.
ideas.experience: Yank a stack trace in Neovim over ssh and a small crystal labelled 'nvim@nas: panic: nil map' breaks off the glass and joins the ring at your shoulder. Drop it on another panel to paste; if it carries newlines headed for a shell prompt it glows red and wants a second click. When a remote tool asks to read your clipboard, the panel says 'wants a crystal' and gets nothing until you raise one.
ideas.audience: Neovim-over-ssh users, security-minded sysadmins, anyone who has pasted the wrong thing into prod
ideas.how: Register GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_CLIPBOARD_WRITE: each GhosttyClipboardWrite carries MIME contents (OSC 52, OSC 1337 Copy or OSC 5522), the program name, granted and can_remember, and is answered inside the callback. Store the crystal (capped with OPT_CLIPBOARD_WRITE_MAX_BYTES) and mirror the chosen one to the desktop with the agent's existing CLIP_SET. OPT_CLIPBOARD_READ must also be answered synchronously, which the agent's round-trip CLIP_GET can't do but a crystal already in memory can: reply SUCCESS with the crystal you're holding out, otherwise DENIED plus a local toast. Dropping a crystal runs ghostty_paste_is_safe (bound today but unused), then ghostty_terminal_paste, so bracketed paste (2004) and kitty paste events (5522) are honoured. Crystals ride the pet springs in lua/world.lua; image/png writes wear a MIME badge until Kitty Graphics Tapestries brings texture upload.
ideas.risks: OSC 52 read is a known way to steal a clipboard, so deny is the default and any remembered grant must be visible and revocable. Many apps never retry a denied read. Crystals hold secrets: memory only, cleared on logout, labels hidden in streamer mode. tmux needs `set-clipboard on`.

ideas.title: Your Feet Are the Mouse
ideas.pitch: Lay a terminal flat on the floor and any mouse-aware TUI follows your character's footsteps as the pointer, with a jump as the click.
ideas.experience: Drop a 12-yalm minesweeper board on your apartment floor and step onto it: the hover highlight follows your boots from tile to tile. Jump and the tile under you flips; land on a mine and the board flashes red around your ankles. A friend who visits sees only you hopping around an empty room.
ideas.audience: housing decorators, TUI game tinkerers, streamers, anyone with a big empty FC house
ideas.how: place() already takes pitch, and world_axes and the depth-pass basis tilt with it, so a `floor` pin lays the panel flat at a Raycast ground height. Each frame ghostty.player() x/z is projected into panel pixels through that basis. The core builds a ghostty_mouse_encoder with setopt_from_terminal, so tracking (1000/1002/1003) and format (SGR 1006, SGR-pixels 1016) come from the app, plus OPT_SIZE and OPT_TRACK_LAST_CELL so motion reports only when you cross a cell. The shim adds ConditionFlag.Jumping to GuObject; its rising edge after a short dwell on a tile sends a button-1 press and release. Stepping on or off the board sends ghostty_focus_encode in or out when mode 1004 is set. Only your own character counts, and only in floor mode.
ideas.risks: The plugin has never reported a click to a TUI (termview only encodes the wheel), so this is the mouse encoder's first user. Jumps are noisy, hence the dwell. Floors aren't flat everywhere, so raycast the corners and refuse slopes, and a flat panel may z-fight the floor in the depth test. Other players' positions must never become input.

ideas.title: Emoji Pyrotechnics
ideas.pitch: Sparkle, party-popper and fire emoji printed by your tools burst out of their exact cell as particle effects that spill into the room.
ideas.experience: Your test runner prints its party popper and confetti rains out of that cell, bouncing on the floor around the panel. `cargo` sparkles send glitter drifting past your ear, and a log line with a fire emoji sheds embers that vanish behind the pillar in front of you. Scroll back over them and nothing fires again: each emoji gets one show.
ideas.audience: streamers, JS and Rust developers, gitmoji fans, chat-TUI users
ideas.how: After Session:feed, walk the render state with ghostty_render_state_row_iterator_next_dirty and read GHOSTTY_RENDER_STATE_ROW_CELLS_DATA_GRAPHEMES_UTF8 per cell, matching a table in a new lua/pyro.lua that maps a grapheme to an emitter preset. Grapheme clustering (mode 2027) keeps ZWJ and VS16 sequences in one cell, so a flag or a skin-toned emoji is a single emitter. Each hit pins its row with a capped ghostty_terminal_grid_ref_track so redraws and scrolling don't refire it, and bursts during reattach replay are skipped the way core/bell.nelua skips replayed bells. Cell rects map to world space through world_transform_vertices; particles are quads through the depth-pass callbacks, landing at one Raycast per burst.
ideas.risks: Dalamud's 16-bit ImWchar can't draw emoji outside the BMP, so most source cells still show tofu and the particles are shapes, not glyphs. Emoji-heavy output such as a gitmoji log needs a per-second budget. TUIs that clear and redraw make old emoji look new. Needs a photosensitivity switch, and emitters stay off in duties.

ideas.title: Waymarked Scrollback
ideas.pitch: Your last eight commands stand on the floor as waymarks A to D and 1 to 4, and stepping onto one scrolls the panel to that command's output.
ideas.experience: After a long debugging session eight markers fan out in front of your panel, green for clean exits and red for failures. Step onto red 3 and the panel scrolls back to `terraform plan` and outlines its output. Alt-drag the marker away and that output tears off as a frozen page, colours intact, that you stick on the wall beside the fix. A healer watching the same session drops marker A on a stack trace, and it rides that line on your copy as new output pours in.
ideas.audience: developers, SREs, on-call rotations inside FCs, anyone who scrolls up hunting for which run failed
ideas.how: The core walks history with ghostty_terminal_grid_ref and GHOSTTY_ROW_DATA_SEMANTIC_PROMPT to find prompt rows and pins each with ghostty_terminal_grid_ref_track, so markers survive scrolling and reflow; when ghostty_tracked_grid_ref_has_value goes false the row was pruned and the marker crumbles. libghostty-vt parses the OSC 133 exit code but doesn't keep it, so colours come from the agent-side CMD_END frame proposed in Commands Cast Like Spells. Standing on a marker (distance from ghostty.player()) calls scroll_viewport with ROW and ghostty_terminal_select_output on the tracked ref. Tearing off formats that selection with ghostty_terminal_selection_format_alloc in VT format and feeds it into a transport-less, read-only terminal pinned like any panel. Shared marks are a MARK frame carrying the line text and output byte offset; each viewer resolves it with ghostty_search_* and tracks the hit.
ideas.risks: Needs shell integration on every host, through ssh and tmux. Tracked refs add work on every update, so cap them. These are drawn markers only plugin users see: never place real waymarks, which the whole party sees. Repeated log lines can resolve a shared mark to the wrong row, and a late joiner whose 256 KiB replay lost the line can't place it. Torn-off pages keep whatever secrets were printed.

categories.name: Familiars
categories.tagline: AI agents that work beside you, report in character and wait politely for the pull to end.

ideas.title: Your Agents Are a Light Party
ideas.pitch: Parallel Claude Code agents fight at your side as a light party: tank plans, healer reviews, two DPS implement in their own worktrees, with context as MP and every tool call as a cast.
ideas.experience: `/term party refactor-loader` and four pet terminals rez into formation: planner out front, reviewer behind you, implementers on your flanks. The party list reads 'DPS, wt/loader-a, Casting: Edit loader.nelua' while MP drains as context fills, and a member waiting for permission pulses with an exclamation mark. When both DPS branches go green a Limit Break gauge fills for a merge you run yourself. Share the party with your FC and members who log in find it working at the workshop bench.
ideas.audience: developers running several AI coding agents at once, developer FCs, raiders who think in roles
ideas.how: `ghostty-party` reads a composition from lua/party.lua (role, job icon, prompt file, worktree), runs `git worktree add` per member, and OPENs `claude` with a CWD env entry and a GHOSTTY_SESSION variable. Claude Code hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Notification, PreCompact, Stop, SubagentStop) call a tiny `ghostty-emit` that writes to a new unix socket on ghostty-agent, which buffers EVENT frames for detached sessions and broadcasts them; MP comes from the last usage entry in the hook's transcript_path. Formation is a new anchor preset on the pet springs in lua/world.lua, and frames are ImGui with job icons from ITextureProvider.GetFromGameIcon. Agents running outside Ghostty join through an in-game MCP server plugin: the shim subscribes to that plugin's agent-board IPC and change event and turns its status posts into frames. The LB button only types `git merge` into the tank's session with `/term type`, never Enter.
ideas.risks: Four live agents cost real money and quota, so the party list shows spend. Hook payloads and tool names change between Claude Code releases. Sharing with the FC puts code, prompts and secrets on other clients, and every attached client can write today, so it needs a read-only relay, a share toggle and redaction. Worktrees pile up and need an explicit disband. Inside duties the formation collapses to frames only. No in-game MCP server has been observed working yet.

ideas.title: Ready Checks for Your Agents
ideas.pitch: When an agent needs you mid-duty it waits for the wipe or the kill, and then every pending question arrives at once as a ready check.
ideas.experience: Queued in Limsa, a local echo line tagged [Ghostty] pops up: 'Claude on bazzite-sway: pin the base image digest, or keep floating stable?' Click it and its panel slides in beside you. Mid-pull two more agents stall without a sound. The boss dies, and a Ready Check window lists all three, each with the last lines of its prompt and its numbered choices; you tick 1, 1 and 3 before the loot rolls finish.
ideas.audience: developers who leave agents running while they play, raiders, on-call devs
ideas.how: Claude Code's Notification and Stop hooks send `ghostty-emit waiting` (the EVENT frame from Your Agents Are a Light Party); other agents can use OSC 9 or 777, which reach GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION once session.nelua registers it. Out of combat the shim prints the line with IChatGui.Print and a link payload that focuses the session's panel; while InCombat or BoundByDuty is set, lines queue. The Ready Check opens on ICondition.ConditionChange (combat off) or IDutyState.DutyWiped and DutyCompleted, as a local window styled after the game's, never the real /readycheck. Each row renders the session's bottom rows from render state, options are parsed from lines shaped like `1. Yes`, and a click sends only that digit through the key encoder to that session. CLAUDE.md can also tell agents to call an in-game MCP server's duty-state tool before asking and keep working while you're inside.
ideas.risks: One-click approvals between pulls is how you approve an `rm -rf` without reading it, so rows show the full command and destructive patterns can't be answered from the check. Parsing Claude Code's prompt off the screen breaks when its TUI changes. Local lines must never look like a real player's tell, both for clarity and honest screenshots. Nothing is ever sent to other players.

ideas.title: Feed It to the Familiar
ideas.pitch: Alt-drag a failing terminal onto your AI companion and it swallows the last command's output as context and starts on the fix.
ideas.experience: `cargo test` just went red on the panel by the window. Alt-grab it, carry it across the room and let go over the Claude pet at your shoulder: the panel folds into it with a gulp of light, then springs back to the wall. The pet's input box reads '[Pasted text: cargo test in ~/cascadia, exit 101, 212 lines]', and a moment later its cast bar says 'Reading main/cascadia-tools/solver.go'.
ideas.audience: developers pairing with Claude Code or other terminal agents
ideas.how: world.drop(id, pose) already fires when an Alt-drag ends (core/policy.nelua:544); lua/world.lua checks the drop point against panels whose profile has `familiar = true`. The core scans GHOSTTY_ROW_DATA_SEMANTIC_PROMPT upward for the last OSC 133 prompt, takes a grid ref on the output after it, calls ghostty_terminal_select_output and ghostty_terminal_selection_format_alloc (plain, unwrapped, trimmed, capped to the tail). A header adds DATA_TITLE, DATA_PWD from OSC 7, the command from INPUT-semantic cells and the exit code from the agent's CMD_END frame. The block goes through ghostty_paste_encode into the familiar's session as a bracketed paste. Without OSC 133 it falls back to a PLAIN formatter over the viewport. The swallow reuses the present and fly-in tween in worldview.nelua.
ideas.risks: It sends terminal output, env dumps and tokens in stderr included, to a hosted model: show a byte count, redact token-shaped strings, confirm the first time. If the familiar sits in a permission prompt the paste lands in the wrong place, so drops are refused unless its last hook state is idle. The source shell needs OSC 133 through tmux and ssh. Alt-drag already means move, so drop targets need a clear highlight.
